(def ^:private pr-writer
  "Prefer this to pr-seq, because it makes the printing function
   configurable, allowing efficient implementations such as appending
   to a StringBuffer."
  (fn [obj writer opts]
  (if-let [alt-impl (:alt-impl opts)]
    (alt-impl obj writer (-assoc opts :fallback-impl pr-writer-impl))
    ;; Clojure's pr-on: a print-method or print-dup method prints obj (#302).
    (if-let [method (print-method-for obj (pr-opts-dup opts))]
      (method obj writer)
      (pr-writer-impl obj writer opts)))))
rationale: Expand the complete pinned defn declaration to def/fn, preserving documentation, visibility, every signature and branch. Retain empty handling, protocol printing, alternate implementation/fallback options and buffer flush/return order. The complete default pr-writer-impl is retained, but its remaining host/storage dependencies are unfinished; calls to unfinished dependencies must fail visibly, never return fabricated output. This is partial source porting, not printing compatibility. Each value prints as Clojure's pr-on prints it (#302): under *print-dup*, with a print-dup method, else, except for a record, as Clojure's print-dup methods for its own types do, with a print-method method; the method is chosen by core's appendix (print-method-for). A value with no method of its own prints with pr-writer-impl and the caller's options. Methods take the value and the writer, as Clojure's do, and read the options from the dynamic vars.
